Nel carcinoma dell'esofago la TC con con:
In esophageal carcinoma, contrast-enhanced CT is used mainly for distant staging (liver, lungs, adrenals, bones, celiac and supraclavicular lymph nodes) and for the relationships with the aorta, trachea-bronchi and pericardium. The T category is better defined with endoscopic ultrasound; PET-CT looks for occult metastases.

Useful CT signs: normal esophageal wall thickness is under 5 mm; the tumor causes asymmetric or circumferential thickening with a narrowed lumen and often upstream dilatation. For the aorta, a contact angle greater than 90° suggests invasion (T4b); for the tracheobronchial tree, indentation or bulging of the posterior wall matters; for the pericardium, loss of the fat plane with indentation of the left atrium (T4a). Absence of a fat plane alone is poorly specific, especially in thin patients.

Squamous cell carcinoma usually affects the mid-upper esophagus (smoking and alcohol), adenocarcinoma the distal esophagus and the junction (reflux, Barrett).

In this case histology showed a G1 squamous cell carcinoma of the middle third, pT4 N0 M0 (AJCC 7th), with residual tumor after surgery (R2).
